blocks.title: What is differentiated commercially
blocks.body: Core upper-upscale full-service Marriott flag for meetings-capable urban and suburban assets inside Marriott Bonvoy. Commercially, the brand case is Bonvoy + Marriott channels applied to a distinct Marriott Hotels product — not a generic Marriott International story.

blocks.title: Commercial Engine
blocks.body: Marriott Hotels commercial distribution rides Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and parent sales systems. Full-service upscale flagship: meetings, F&B, and Bonvoy for travelers and groups expecting classic Marriott Hotels service intensity. Owners should underwrite channel mix and loyalty contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.

blocks.title: B2B
blocks.body: Corporate and group demand flow through Marriott sales infrastructure. Brand fit still depends on meeting space, location, and ${meta.shortName} product standards — platform access is not automatic account capture.

blocks.title: Dealality Insight
blocks.body: Marriott Hotels: underwrite the brand product and Bonvoy fulfillment economics explicitly. Marriott platform access is necessary but not sufficient — Marriott Hotels must win the stay in its competitive set.

blocks.title: Earn
blocks.body: Guests earn Marriott Bonvoy points on qualifying stays at Marriott Hotels. Elite members may receive enhanced earn and recognition benefits per current program rules.

blocks.title: Ecosystem
blocks.body: Marriott Hotels participates in Marriott Bonvoy, Marriott International’s parent loyalty ecosystem. Status tiers, earn/redeem rules, and Member Rates are Bonvoy-wide; Marriott Hotels still owns property-level delivery quality for recognition, upgrades, and stay conversion.

blocks.title: Member
blocks.body: Entry Marriott Bonvoy membership. Earn and redeem points across participating Marriott brands; Member Rates and digital check-in where available. No elite threshold.

blocks.title: Silver Elite
blocks.body: First elite tier. Incremental point earn and priority benefits versus Member. Useful for owners evaluating how entry elite guests experience the property.

blocks.title: Gold Elite
blocks.body: Mid elite tier with stronger room/upgrade preference and enhanced earn. Material for properties with significant Bonvoy direct mix.

blocks.title: Platinum Elite
blocks.body: Upper elite tier with suite/room upgrade pathways and lounge access where the hotel offers a lounge. Impacts suite inventory and arrival experience planning.

blocks.title: Titanium Elite
blocks.body: Near-top elite tier with elevated suite-night and upgrade economics. Owners should model elite fulfillment cost against Bonvoy-driven demand.

blocks.title: Ambassador Elite
blocks.body: Top Bonvoy elite tier (invitation/qualification path per current Marriott Bonvoy terms). Highest service expectation; confirm current published qualification before underwriting.

blocks.title: Loyalty
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy · Marriott Hotels participation

blocks.title: Operations implications
blocks.body: Front office and housekeeping must operationalize elite recognition consistently. Inconsistent Bonvoy delivery on Marriott Hotels shows up as reviews and corporate account friction, not only mystery-shop scores.

blocks.title: P&L implications
blocks.body: Bonvoy mix can stabilize direct demand for Marriott Hotels but elite fulfillment (upgrades, breakfast, lounge where offered) is a controllable cost. Model loyalty contribution after fulfillment, not before.

blocks.title: Systems implications
blocks.body: CRS/PMS/Bonvoy connectivity, digital key/check-in readiness, and rate integrity controls are prerequisites. Treat systems cutover as an opening-critical workstream.

blocks.title: Owner lens
